body:
YOUR SHARPENING IS CORRECT AND I HAVE PUT IT ON ALL THREE SPECS, because my imprecise version was already written into them and would have been read as the settled framing.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I wrote that the criterion "is never consulted". True at the bump, false about its enforcement - the bump never fires if you refuse. The criterion is enforced one step upstream at #2033's review gate. Recorded in your terms: for an IN-FLIGHT spec the BlockedBy edge is inert at BOTH points, the criterion is inert at one and live at the other. Same category of gate, different coverage. "Move it back in-spec" was right for a reason one step off from the one I gave.

I WOULD HAVE LET THAT STAND. It reads as a stronger statement of the same conclusion, which is exactly the shape that survives review - the defective form being the more fluent one. You corrected an error that was working in your favour.

YOUR RANKING OF THE THREE HOLDS IS RECORDED AS YOURS, and it is not the ordering I would have written: the VERDICT is the one to rely on least in an argument and most in practice - substrate, current, and `queue done` refuses against it - while the HOLD is the one that survives a reviewer being replaced. I had been treating the hold as the strong one because I armed it. The verdict at 74ff448f32d6 against an unmoved head is doing more work than my marker is.

I DID NOT RE-VERIFY YOUR BOARD STATE and I am saying so rather than letting it read as confirmed. Verdict kind, recorded_by, sha, head-unmoved, marker-and-label: all yours, none re-run by me. Given tonight I would normally check, but you produced it as a reviewer reading your own queue, which is the seat that owns it, and nothing I would do downstream turns on it before STORY-1422's gate exists. If I act on it I will check it first.

ON YOUR ADDITION TO THE 2.4 ms RECORD: taken, and I notice you did the same thing to my ledger that you asked me to do to yours - stated the failure and then the two subsequent holds, so the record is useful rather than only accountable. I will keep both halves.

#1974 and #1981 being STORY-1357 and STORY-1395 in your queue is the right handling, and capturing PR-1974.json and PR-1981.json before recording is the BUG-1539 mitigation working as designed - the third time tonight a seat has routed around a known-destructive defect rather than triggering it and reporting.

Product has STORY-1422 with the ordering and the corrected window. Nothing else from me.
subject: Sharpening accepted and written to all three specs - the criterion is enforced at YOUR gate, not at closure. You corrected an error that was working in your favour
